bull_bear.body: Organic capex for capacity expansion; Talent acquisition (business heads for verticals); No plans to demerge New Age vertical despite D2C valuation premiums, citing integrated farm-to-brand model efficiency.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Milk price volatility (currently INR42/l, stable short-term); Input cost inflation (packaging, fuel); Core category volume pressure from pricing actions; Dependency on quick commerce growth for New Age segment.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; Emphasizes 'pivotal year' with measurable outcomes; Disciplined on profitability over blind volume growth; Transparent on one-offs (remuneration, incentives).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Inventory increase of INR150cr is entirely rate-driven (inflation) with nil quantitative buildup, indicating no channel stuffing; New Age business margins are ~2x company average but suppressed sequentially in Q4 due to deliberate promotion withdrawal to stabilize profitability; Government incentive drop structural due to GST rate cut (12% to 5%) not operational failure.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet de-leveraging: net debt falls across FY23-FY26 as 539, 540, 561, 484 (₹ Cr) against net worth of 808, 912, 1,023, 1,259 (₹ Cr); the deck states net debt "now stands at ₹484 Cr" in FY26.
- Leverage ratios improve over FY23-FY26: Net Debt/Equity 0.7 → 0.6 → 0.5 → 0.4 and Net Debt/EBITDA 3.3 → 2.4 → 1.9 → 1.6.
- Return ratios over FY23-FY26: ROCE 8.6% → 11.1% → 14.3% → 13.9% and ROE 7.8% → 10.5% → 12.3% → 11.8%; the deck describes FY26 as "healthy return ratios (ROCE at 13.9%, ROE at 11.8%)".
- Cashflow from operations over FY23-FY26: -190, 102, 212, 149 (₹ Cr); the deck's own commentary says "Cashflow from operations grew steadily to ₹149 Cr", which sits against its own series showing FY25 at 212.
- Working capital (days of sales) FY23-FY26: Inventory 72, 72, 61, 70; Receivables 21, 28, 28, 23; NWC 74, 75, 62, 68.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- integration: milk-to-finished-product value chain owned from farm procurement to branded retail — evidence: 5 lakh+ dairy farmers, 2,400+ village collection centres across 5 states, 300+ bulk milk coolers/chilling centres, own automated Bhagyalaxmi farm with 5,000+ cows — against it: MD&A says industry-wide inflation in milk procurement prices pressured gross margins, particularly in commoditised segments, and hit liquid-milk profitability
- distribution: pan-India route to market — evidence: 4,500+ distributors, 500+ super stockists, 29 depots and 4.6 lakh retail touchpoints
- scale: large dairy processing base — evidence: 34 lakh litres per day milk handling capacity across Manchar, Thorandale and Palamaner; 110 MT per day cheese and ghee production; 10 lakh litres per day whey processing
- brand: category share in branded cow ghee and cheese — evidence: AR prints 22% and 35% market share for Gowardhan Ghee (branded cow ghee segment) and Go Cheese (cheese segment); core categories ghee, cheese and paneer are ~60% of revenue
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw milk price volatility — The company flags price volatility in raw materials, especially milk, as a cost and margin risk; it mitigates through long-term supply contracts, supplier diversification, market tracking and strategic sourcing.
- Food quality and safety — Non-compliance with safety protocols can damage brand credibility for a branded consumer dairy business; mitigated via training, regular audits, incident reporting and continuous improvement.
- Product redundancy / changing consumer needs — Evolving consumer needs require constant innovation; the company relies on market research, trend analysis, R&D and agile product development to keep its portfolio relevant.
- Competition — High industry competition is flagged as a growth challenge; response is competitive pricing, market responsiveness and a differentiated value proposition.
- Macroeconomic factors — Inflation, currency fluctuations and political changes can affect operations; mitigated by economic monitoring, agile strategy adjustment and a diversified contract manufacturing model.
- Compliance, regulatory and reputation — Legal or regulatory non-compliance can erode brand value; addressed through continuous legal monitoring, risk assessments and compliance processes.
- Contract / client performance — Failure to meet client expectations can result in penalties and reputational loss; mitigated through quality checks, communication, execution and periodic audits.
- People / talent — Talent acquisition and retention are described as critical for sustained growth; mitigated through targeted recruitment, training and career growth opportunities.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims a "# 2 position" in cheese with "35% Market share (source IMARC)" and a "# 1 position" in cow ghee, described as "Leaders and pioneers in cow ghee category" with "22% Market share in branded cow ghee segment (source IMARC)".
- Founded 1992 by Mr. Devendra Shah, "strategically located in the milk belt at Manchar"; listed in 2016. Deck frames the strengths as "developed infrastructure, food technology expertise supported by a strong farmer network, and powerful distribution channels".
- Four "power brands" are described by lifestyle positioning: everyday dairy essentials; processed/natural cheese, UHT milk and dairy beverages; a premium farm-to-home single-origin brand; and "India's first Made in India whey protein brand". (The extraction lost the brand-name-to-description binding on this slide; brand names appear elsewhere in the deck as Gowardhan, Go Cheese, Pride of Cows and Avvatar.)
- Avvatar is positioned as the first "Made in India" whey protein brand — "offering unadulterated, fresh, 100% vegetarian whey".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Regulation] Cheese marketing is being aligned with "the latest government regulations mandating the declaration of Real Cheese and Analogue Cheese by food establishments"; the company deployed a "HoReCa Authenticity Certificate".
- [Leadership] "Parag Milk Foods elevates Mr. Rakesh Kothari as Chief Financial Officer and KMP".
- [Ownership] 2021 saw "Investment by International Finance Corporation (IFC) and prominent consumer fund - Sixth Sense Venture Advisors LLP"; Sixth Sense founder Mr. Nikhil Vora sits on the Board as a Non-Executive Director.
- [Marketing] Avvatar partnered with "India's Got Latent Season 2" hosted by Samay Raina, a show with "more than 64 mn views on Youtube and more than 2.2 mn views on Netflix"; a separate campaign slide cites 37 Mn Views and 92 Mn Impressions, and an influencer push cites "40+ Influencers; 3.1 Mn Impressions".
- [Recognition] Executive Director Akshali Shah recognised in "Fortune India's Most Powerful Women in Business 2026"; the deck notes CII Andhra Pradesh safety excellence award and a BIS Certificate of Appreciation for Whole Milk Powder standards.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Parag Milk Foods procures milk from a network of dairy farmers across five southern and western states and processes it at its Manchar, Thorandale and Palamaner facilities into ghee, cheese, paneer, milk, curd, yoghurt, UHT beverages, whey protein, lactose and other value-added dairy and nutrition products. It sells to households through general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce and its own website/app, and to hotels, restaurants, caterers, institutions and large corporates. Its ingredients business supplies pharmaceutical, bakery, confectionery, infant-nutrition and protein-product makers.

- **Core categories (Gowardhan):** Gowardhan ghee (incl. 20 ml sachet), paneer, curd/dahi, butter, fresh milk, flavoured milk, dairy whitener, ready-to-eat sweets, gulab jamun mix
- **Cheese & value-added (Go):** Go cheese slices, cheese spread in tube, flavoured cheese wedges, cheese angles, UHT milk, buttermilk / masala chaas, lassi, flavoured milk shakes, fruit and flavoured yoghurt, Go Slim Milk
- **New Age - premium dairy (Pride of Cows):** single-origin farm-to-home whole milk and low-fat milk, ghee, paneer, low-fat high-protein paneer, curd, Greek yoghurt, whole milk powder

outlook.body: Revenue: Aspiring INR10,000cr long-term; New Age segment target 20-25% of mix (approx INR1,000cr) in 3-5 years; Core category volume growth: Double-digit aspiration for FY27; Margins: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margins medium-term; Capex: INR60-70cr for FY27 (Cheese capacity expansion, lactose/whey plant upgrades).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A for FMCG; Demand signals strong in North/South expansion zones; Cheese capacity utilization high, expanding from 60MT to 80MT soon.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Geographic expansion into North (UP) and South India (30% of population) where penetration is currently low; Shift from unorganized to organized dairy (Ghee/Paneer); New product formats in protein (wafers, Greek yogurt) driving New Age segment to INR1,000cr.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Expand manufacturing capacity ahead of demand to sustain double-digit growth in the foundational categories (ghee, cheese, paneer), scale the new-age nutrition business and shift the mix toward higher-margin products.
- Strengthen manufacturing through automation, AI tools, brownfield expansion, technology integration and process optimisation; projects are underway across value-added dairy, protein and nutrition categories.
- Build new dairy-ingredient capabilities: Milk Protein Concentrate, ready-to-drink protein and pharma-grade lactose, alongside cheese capacity expansion, whey processing expansion and refined lactose capability.
- Invest in packaging solutions and automation (including IQF cheese packaging) for premium and value-added categories.
- Expand the portfolio across value-added dairy, protein and nutrition through consumer-led product development and innovation.
- Brand-specific marketing: Gowardhan via mass TV/regional festive properties; Go toward younger consumers plus B2B and export outreach; Pride of Cows on a traceable single-origin proposition; Avvatar via celebrity, influencer and digital-first campaigns in sports nutrition.
- Improve household penetration and trials among value-conscious consumers, e.g. Gowardhan Ghee in a 20 ml sachet.
- Human capital priorities: talent retention, workforce productivity and a stronger leadership pipeline.
- Reduce resource intensity and move to cleaner energy (solar partnerships, ETP biogas, water reuse).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Parag runs three manufacturing units (Manchar and Thorandale in Maharashtra, Palamaner in Andhra Pradesh) plus two dairy farms. During FY26 it installed a packaging line at Palamaner for beverage/long-shelf-life products, and at Thorandale commissioned a fully automated chikki line, added cheese production and upgraded cold rooms. Stated focus areas include cheese capacity expansion, whey processing expansion, refined lactose capabilities, utility/infrastructure strengthening, an advanced analytical testing laboratory, SCADA process control and packaging automation (including IQF cheese packaging). Milk Protein Concentrate, ready-to-drink protein and pharma-grade lactose capability development is underway, and management says it is expanding capacity ahead of demand through brownfield expansion; projects are underway across value-added dairy, protein and nutrition categories. No commissioning dates are given for these projects. A new 100 KL STP was installed (BRSR).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Consumer preference is shifting toward cheese, paneer, flavoured and fortified milk, probiotic yoghurt and premium ghee, categories with higher margins and faster growth than liquid milk.
- Urban demand for protein-rich products (Greek yoghurt, fortified milk, high-protein cheese) is rising with health and wellness awareness.
- Demand for premium and value-added dairy is expected to remain strong, especially among urban consumers.
- Shift from unbranded to branded dairy as consumers become more quality-aware, favouring organised players; the organised segment is expected to grow on volumes and staggered price increases.
- E-commerce, modern retail and quick commerce are widening access to urban and semi-urban markets.
- Government schemes (Rashtriya Gokul Mission, LHDCP, National Programme for Dairy Development, AHIDF) support cold-chain, cattle productivity and processing investment.
- Dairy alternatives (plant-based) are emerging as a fast-growing segment, helped by lactose-intolerance and environmental concerns.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Parag Milk Foods delivered a pivotal Q4FY26 with gross margins expanding to 28% despite 15% YoY milk inflation, driven by a strategic shift to high-margin 'New Age' brands (Avvatar, Pride of Cows) which now contribute 10% of revenue and grew >100% YoY. While core category volumes dipped 3% due to high-base institutional/export comparables, the structural pivot toward protein and premiumization positions the company for sustained double-digit EBITDA targets as geographic expansion accelerates in North/South India.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Integrated dairy FMCG company selling 100% cow's-milk products under four homegrown brands (Gowardhan, Go, Pride of Cows, Avvatar), with milk processing capacity of 34 lakh litres per day.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Parag Milk Foods procures milk from a network of dairy farmers across five southern and western states and processes it at its Manchar, Thorandale and Palamaner facilities into ghee, cheese, paneer, milk, curd, yoghurt, UHT beverages, whey protein, lactose and other value-added dairy and nutrition products. It sells to households through general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce and its own website/app, and to hotels, restaurants, caterers, institutions and large corporates. Its ingredients business supplies pharmaceutical, bakery, confectionery, infant-nutrition and protein-product makers.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Bhagyalaxmi Dairy Farms Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% subsidiary since December 2, 2003; the Company's Bhagyalaxmi dairy farm houses 5,000+ cows with an automated milking process
- Parag Foods Middle East FZE — subsidiary: Subsidiary w.e.f. January 7, 2025; yet to commence operations
- Poojan Shah — related party: Relative of KMP (listed under remuneration to KMP and their relatives); General Manager - Business Operations holding an office or place of profit, approval sought at the 34th AGM
- Stavan Shah — related party: Listed under remuneration to KMP and their relatives
- Priti Shah — related party: Rent counterparty in the RPT note (company pays rent); relationship not stated in this extract
- Netra Shah — related party: Rent counterparty in the RPT note (company pays rent); relationship not stated in this extract
- Virendra Varma — related party: KMP - Group Secretary & Compliance Officer
- Nitin R. Dhavalikar — related party: Listed under commission to directors in the RPT note; not on the board as of March 31, 2026

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Core Categories (Ghee, Cheese, Paneer): 60% of business, Q4 volume decline 3% (base effect from institutional/export); Ghee market share ~22%; New Age (Avvatar, Pride of Cows): 10% of business, >100% YoY growth, Q4 revenue >INR100cr; Avvatar holds 14-15% share on quick commerce/marketplaces.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Core categories (Gowardhan):** Gowardhan ghee (incl. 20 ml sachet), paneer, curd/dahi, butter, fresh milk, flavoured milk, dairy whitener, ready-to-eat sweets, gulab jamun mix
- **Cheese & value-added (Go):** Go cheese slices, cheese spread in tube, flavoured cheese wedges, cheese angles, UHT milk, buttermilk / masala chaas, lassi, flavoured milk shakes, fruit and flavoured yoghurt, Go Slim Milk
- **New Age - premium dairy (Pride of Cows):** single-origin farm-to-home whole milk and low-fat milk, ghee, paneer, low-fat high-protein paneer, curd, Greek yoghurt, whole milk powder
- **New Age - sports nutrition (Avvatar):** Performance Whey, Isopure Blend, Fuel Whey, Protein Wafer Bar, coffee and matcha protein bars, creatine / micronized creatine
- **Ingredients:** whey, milk powders, lactose / refined lactose

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian retail households via general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce, company website and mobile app
- HoReCa (hotels, restaurants, cafes/catering), institutional and large-format corporate buyers
- Ingredient customers in pharmaceutical formulations, bakery, confectionery, infant nutrition, protein-enriched products and dairy desserts
- Premium metro consumers for Pride of Cows (expanded to additional metros including Chandigarh)
- International market (Palamaner facility produces for domestic and international markets)

capacity.body:

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A for FMCG; Demand signals strong in North/South expansion zones; Cheese capacity utilization high, expanding from 60MT to 80MT soon.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue: Aspiring INR10,000cr long-term; New Age segment target 20-25% of mix (approx INR1,000cr) in 3-5 years; Core category volume growth: Double-digit aspiration for FY27; Margins: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margins medium-term; Capex: INR60-70cr for FY27 (Cheese capacity expansion, lactose/whey plant upgrades).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Geographic expansion into North (UP) and South India (30% of population) where penetration is currently low; Shift from unorganized to organized dairy (Ghee/Paneer); New product formats in protein (wafers, Greek yogurt) driving New Age segment to INR1,000cr.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Consumer preference is shifting toward cheese, paneer, flavoured and fortified milk, probiotic yoghurt and premium ghee, categories with higher margins and faster growth than liquid milk.
- Urban demand for protein-rich products (Greek yoghurt, fortified milk, high-protein cheese) is rising with health and wellness awareness.
- Demand for premium and value-added dairy is expected to remain strong, especially among urban consumers.
- Shift from unbranded to branded dairy as consumers become more quality-aware, favouring organised players; the organised segment is expected to grow on volumes and staggered price increases.
- E-commerce, modern retail and quick commerce are widening access to urban and semi-urban markets.
- Government schemes (Rashtriya Gokul Mission, LHDCP, National Programme for Dairy Development, AHIDF) support cold-chain, cattle productivity and processing investment.
- Dairy alternatives (plant-based) are emerging as a fast-growing segment, helped by lactose-intolerance and environmental concerns.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin expanded to 28% via mix shift and pricing power despite milk prices rising 15% YoY to INR42/litre; EBITDA margin compressed to 8.1% due to elevated employee costs (one-off remuneration/ESOP) and inflation; Management confident of flow-through to double-digit EBITDA as one-offs normalize.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Organic capex for capacity expansion; Talent acquisition (business heads for verticals); No plans to demerge New Age vertical despite D2C valuation premiums, citing integrated farm-to-brand model efficiency.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Parag runs three manufacturing units (Manchar and Thorandale in Maharashtra, Palamaner in Andhra Pradesh) plus two dairy farms. During FY26 it installed a packaging line at Palamaner for beverage/long-shelf-life products, and at Thorandale commissioned a fully automated chikki line, added cheese production and upgraded cold rooms. Stated focus areas include cheese capacity expansion, whey processing expansion, refined lactose capabilities, utility/infrastructure strengthening, an advanced analytical testing laboratory, SCADA process control and packaging automation (including IQF cheese packaging). Milk Protein Concentrate, ready-to-drink protein and pharma-grade lactose capability development is underway, and management says it is expanding capacity ahead of demand through brownfield expansion; projects are underway across value-added dairy, protein and nutrition categories. No commissioning dates are given for these projects. A new 100 KL STP was installed (BRSR).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic; Emphasizes 'pivotal year' with measurable outcomes; Disciplined on profitability over blind volume growth; Transparent on one-offs (remuneration, incentives).

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "Contingent-liability note (Note 41, consolidated) lists sales tax, GST and income-tax matters under litigation plus a corporate guarantee for a vendor-financing programme; the Group states no pending matter is expected to have a material adverse effect on its financial statements.", "as_of": "2026-09-05"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: milk-to-finished-product value chain owned from farm procurement to branded retail — evidence: 5 lakh+ dairy farmers, 2,400+ village collection centres across 5 states, 300+ bulk milk coolers/chilling centres, own automated Bhagyalaxmi farm with 5,000+ cows — against it: MD&A says industry-wide inflation in milk procurement prices pressured gross margins, particularly in commoditised segments, and hit liquid-milk profitability
- distribution: pan-India route to market — evidence: 4,500+ distributors, 500+ super stockists, 29 depots and 4.6 lakh retail touchpoints
- scale: large dairy processing base — evidence: 34 lakh litres per day milk handling capacity across Manchar, Thorandale and Palamaner; 110 MT per day cheese and ghee production; 10 lakh litres per day whey processing
- brand: category share in branded cow ghee and cheese — evidence: AR prints 22% and 35% market share for Gowardhan Ghee (branded cow ghee segment) and Go Cheese (cheese segment); core categories ghee, cheese and paneer are ~60% of revenue

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Milk price volatility (currently INR42/l, stable short-term); Input cost inflation (packaging, fuel); Core category volume pressure from pricing actions; Dependency on quick commerce growth for New Age segment.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Inventory increase of INR150cr is entirely rate-driven (inflation) with nil quantitative buildup, indicating no channel stuffing; New Age business margins are ~2x company average but suppressed sequentially in Q4 due to deliberate promotion withdrawal to stabilize profitability; Government incentive drop structural due to GST rate cut (12% to 5%) not operational failure.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand manufacturing capacity ahead of demand to sustain double-digit growth in the foundational categories (ghee, cheese, paneer), scale the new-age nutrition business and shift the mix toward higher-margin products.
- Strengthen manufacturing through automation, AI tools, brownfield expansion, technology integration and process optimisation; projects are underway across value-added dairy, protein and nutrition categories.
- Build new dairy-ingredient capabilities: Milk Protein Concentrate, ready-to-drink protein and pharma-grade lactose, alongside cheese capacity expansion, whey processing …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulation] Cheese marketing is being aligned with "the latest government regulations mandating the declaration of Real Cheese and Analogue Cheese by food establishments"; the company deployed a "HoReCa Authenticity Certificate".
- [Leadership] "Parag Milk Foods elevates Mr. Rakesh Kothari as Chief Financial Officer and KMP".
- [Ownership] 2021 saw "Investment by International Finance Corporation (IFC) and prominent consumer fund - Sixth Sense Venture Advisors LLP"; Sixth Sense founder Mr. Nikhil Vora sits on the Board as a Non-Executive Director.
- [Marketing] Avvatar partnered with "India's Got Latent Season 2" hosted by Samay Raina, a show with "more than 64 mn views on Youtube and more than 2.2 mn views on Netflix"; a separate campaign slide cites 37 Mn Views and 92 Mn Impressions, and an influencer push cites "40+ Influencers; 3.1 Mn Impressions".
- [Recognition] Executive Director Akshali Shah recognised in "Fortune India's Most Powerful Women in Business 2026"; the deck notes CII Andhra Pradesh safety excellence award and a BIS Certificate of Appreciation for Whole Milk Powder standards.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

themes.title: Agri value-chain - food processing, dairy, protein & seeds
themes.need: Rising protein/processed-food consumption, animal-nutrition demand and export tailwinds drive an integrated agri value-chain - DODLA/PARAGMILK on dairy; AVANTIFEED/SHINDL/SKMEGGPROD/HMAAGRO on aqua/poultry/meat protein; GODREJAGRO/KSCL/NATHBIOGEN on feed + seeds; REGAAL/SUKHJITS/GULPOLY on maize/starch; FOODSIN/MANORAMA on agri-processing & specialty fats.
themes.driver: Monsoon-led farm income; protein export demand; feed-margin recovery; festive processed-food restocking.
